text: TWILIGHT SITTING 2026-09-26: THE TOP-THREE FRAMING IS REJECTED AND REPLACED BY A BETTER MECHANIC. Owner typed the above. What it establishes: (a) A SKYLIGHT DRIFTS OVER ABOUT A WEEK, not over years as the frozen sheet and both design passes assumed. That is a playable cadence a colony actually experiences, not background lore. It supersedes the sheet's 'every light-well is temporary on a years scale' timing while leaving hard ban 5 (no permanent skylight) intact. (b) THERE ARE OTHER LIGHTS THE PLAYER GROWS SLOWLY THEMSELVES - the sun-sphere / ollumin culture line. (c) 🔑 THE LOAD-BEARING INSIGHT, his: 'and this explains the movable chained floating fields.' The tethered cage farms are movable BECAUSE the light moves. Chain a floating field and walk it to follow the drifting shaft, or culture your own light and stay put. That fuses two previously separate ideas into one trade and gives the biome its arc: early game you chase the light, late game you make it and become independent of the Compact's leases. (d) It also DISSOLVES a conflict the review sheet had filed as its own row - 'the sun-sphere frees the player from the skylight economy' vs 'skylight tenancy is the #1 marquee'. Not a conflict: that IS the progression. (e) A week-long drift also rescales skylight tenancy: a Compact lease is short-term and renewed, not generational. ⇒ NO ranked top three. He asked to 'explore the others more dynamically' - the remaining four (dry river as travel lane, the gardener's events, living light, charts and ledgers) are open for design, not queued behind a fixed 1-2-3.

title: The bedazzle program: eleven biomes raised to the Baroque bar in ruled order (Contagion first, Black Crags last), four-movement ritual, nine-mark bar as the design gate; all other biomes grandfathered subject to the gate
ownerSaid: Bedazzle means we take what's there and review, fill the flora/fauna roster, then start ideating what could be REALLY awesome/unique mechanics. text: Owner's authoritative history of ExplosiveGrowth intent; next: consensus review.
ownerSaid: To be clear: the original design was simply me saying the dry-adapted alien plants of this world generally barely grow at all until they get access to water, then they grow x10 speed to take advantage of it. That's what I originally meant by explosive growth. You heard that and misinterpreted it to mean they actually detonate, and I thought that was fascinating as a concept. So we accepted the exploratory idea that the plants grow and grow until at peak maturity they sometimes burst/die, resulting in many additional sprouts surrounding them. This was later adapted to a reduced growth factor in permanently wet areas and making fruit instead of bursting. I hope that clarifies the discussion that's been happening. Now we need to do a review of what's been planned and implemented here to bring everyone into consensus together.

text: Owner rulings 2026-10-18 card: (1) shallow drowning stays default-on. ownerSaid: Drown slowly, keep default [shallows drowning stays on]. PIT ROOM: the superdeep came from the observation that a human can lift their arms up and pull themselves out of a pit. It needs to be deep enough that an athletic human could not reasonably raise their arms over their head and jump a little to grab the edge, then scramble up the side. Use that rule to determine. PAINTED PONDS: if the source is effectively infinite (huge in map, or extends off map, or a river) then it does not get a sloped floor. We should stick with that. We will work out appearance matching later. HOSE LEFTOVER: yes, and it's not just filth, it's spilled water as per wetting the ground, plant growth, etc.

ownerSaid: Let's talk about this. A very large creature (say 10 cell) may see a narrow slot in a wall as 'something way down there, I don't care' and simply walk over a wall, damaging the wall as though it were an object. This would not be true of a thin passage through a mountain. If a large creature is trapped by thin wooden walls around it, it walks through them effortlessly; if the walls were as thick as it is, no longer. I like squeezing through logic if at least half its width: slowing, not a stop. Do a design pass for the options so we can have different ideas for maximum game fun. Do a GPT review of your idea. Likely also involves whether the building is roofed or not: a free-standing thin unroofed wall is easier to smash than a roofed one.

This should allow pawns to scale walls (unroofed on both sides) just as easily as canal sides, albeit slowly. Then jump packs and other leaping abilities allow entrance/exit immediately, and teleportation, etc.

Please commission that as art and as a review sheet item to watch work.

title: Sluice gate: lifts up to open, toggled from an adjacent cell, god-mode force open/close, open/closed graphics, open=traversable closed=not
ownerSaid: Needing a colonist to "walk" through a sluice gate to re-open it makes no sense. A colonist should be able to open/close a sluice gate while standing "next" to it and above or below without walking down to it. And there should be a debug/god-mode click button to force open or closed. Your art for "open" is wrong: it never opens. Sluice gates do not open by sliding left/right, they slide "up" to allow the water through. Needs to have an Open graphic and a Closed graphic like the ladders on the walls. When closed, it is not traversible. When open it is.
